changes: Purpose rephrased as a short gloss instead of copying the raw colophon string
Notes expanded: the date and scribe come from the colophon of the first text (1st foliation) only; the Gurustotra colophon (2nd foliation) has no date or scribe of its own
Sahajānanda kept as a low-confidence beneficiary, with a note that the word may just mean 'innate bliss' and not be a person

purpose: dedicatory wish at the end of the Gurustotra: may the Guru be pleased, for (or on behalf of) Sahajānanda
notes: The era is not named ('saṃvat 840'). It is taken as NS because the script is Newari, the Newari phrase 'thva kuhnu' is used, and the catalogue says NS 840. NS 840 = c. 1720 CE (Āṣāḍha pūrṇimā, around June/July 1720). The weekday has not been checked. The date and the scribe Purarāja ('vipra' = brahmin) come from the colophon of the Gurusahasranāmastotra (1st foliation). The Gurustotra (2nd foliation, ascribed to the Rudrayāmala) has no date or scribe of its own, so it may or may not be by the same hand. 'sahajānaṃdāya' (dative) could be the initiate name of the owner or patron, for whom the Guru's favour is asked. It could also just be the abstract term 'innate bliss' (sahajānanda), with no person meant, so p2 is uncertain. 'prīṇātu⟨ḥ⟩': the cataloguer marks the visarga as wrong.
